# The storyboard

The third stop: the script of the whole page, which the person says yes to. Write it to `docs/story/storyboard.md`.

A plan covers what its asker thought to ask for. Most people ask for the idea and for what moves. Nobody asks what the site does on a phone, or without the 3D, or what a shared link shows, and a script that leaves those out is half a script. So this one has a place for each, and an empty place shows.

## The chapters

A row to a chapter:

| Chapter | Its name in the form | The role it holds | What it tells, in a few words | What the pieces do | What you can touch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## The beats

Under each chapter, a row to a beat. A beat is one settled state of the scene and one block of text.

| Beat | Screens | How the pieces stand | What is on their faces | What the chapter adds | What its caption stands on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- **Screens:** how much scroll the beat takes. One, or more where the scroll works something.
- **How the pieces stand:** a stack, a fan, a ring, a row, a wall, or what the chapter needs. The same pieces in every beat.
- **What is on their faces:** the person's real pictures and words. Name the picture.
- **What the chapter adds:** anything in the scene besides the pieces. Often nothing.
- **What its caption stands on:** a working title of a few words, and the lines of the fact sheet the caption will be written from. Not the caption.

**Write no captions yet.** The words are written at a later stop, where the person chooses them. A sentence written now, to make the script read well, is where a detail gets in that nobody told you: a hall that was "standing empty", a wheel that is "true again". So a beat names its facts and stops there. Where a beat wants something the fact sheet does not hold, such as what the work taught them or what was wrong before they came, put the question in its place.

## Someone with thirty seconds

Say how a visitor who does not scroll gets the name, what the person does, one proof of it, and how to reach them. The first screen carries the first three. A rail jumps to any chapter, and one link skips to the close.

## Without the scene

Say what a visitor gets in each case. The text is ordinary HTML over the scene, so all of it is there in every row. Say what stands in for the pieces.

| Where | What the visitor gets |
|---|---|
| On a phone | |
| With reduced motion | |
| With no WebGL | |
| With no JavaScript | |

## The look and the type

Both come from the object's material: plates are ceramic on linen, a status page is dark glass, a paper is white with dark ink. Name two or three looks, each as its ground, its ink, one accent, and the surface of the pieces. The person picks by scrolling, once it is built.

Two typefaces: one for the text, and one for what is printed on the pieces, which belongs to the form.

## Everything else the site needs

Mark every row build, later or never, and say who decided.

| | Build, later or never | Who decided |
|---|---|---|
| The way round the page | | |
| A page for each project | | |
| Every project listed | | |
| How to reach them, and a CV | | |
| What others say | | |
| Languages | | |
| What a shared link shows, and the site's icon | | |
| The page for an address that is not there | | |
| A blog | | |
| A chat | | |
| A legal notice, where their country asks for one | | |

## What you ask for

A yes to the script, or what to change. Give the list of what you decided for them with it.

# Ines Okafor — source facts

Original source statements below are supplemented and, where necessary, superseded by the user confirmations beside them. Silence does not confirm the remaining statements. Sources: `material/linkedin.md` (saved October 2026) and `material/notes.md`. No website has been built or visual concept selected.

## Identity and practice

- F01: Ines Okafor; Head Chef at Saltmarsh; Leeds, England. Focus: fermentation, whole-vegetable cooking, apprentices. Source: linkedin.md, heading.
- F02: Saltmarsh is a 40-seat restaurant in Leeds. Ines cares about work before service and using trim, whey, stems and bones; the kitchen has a jar wall and a prep list longer than the menu. Source: linkedin.md, About.
- F03: Ines runs an apprentice programme and writes Brine, a small preserving zine. Source: linkedin.md, About.

## Work and education

- F04: Head Chef, Saltmarsh, March 2022–present; menu changes weekly. Source: linkedin.md, Experience. Notes say Ines took over the kitchen in September 2022; distinction unresolved. User confirms: acting head chef from March 2022; formal Head Chef from September 2022. Use September 2022 for Head Chef. This resolves the discrepancy.
- F05: Kitchen food waste reduced from 14 kg to 5 kg per week. Measurement method, comparison periods and personal/team attribution unknown. Source: linkedin.md, Saltmarsh. User confirms: whole kitchen, prep and plate waste, weighed over one month in 2023. Say “we”. Bones were excluded because they go to stock. Exact comparison windows within the month remain unspecified; do not imply ongoing measured performance.
- F06: Built a larder with 40+ ferments, vinegars and garums on rotation. Counting basis, period and collaborators unknown. Source: linkedin.md, Saltmarsh.
- F07: Two apprentices a year since 2023. Intake versus completion and exact responsibility unconfirmed. Source: linkedin.md, Saltmarsh.
- F08: Sous Chef, The Corn Exchange Kitchen, Leeds, June 2019–February 2022; ran the pass on a 90-cover service; took over ordering and reduced supplier list from 31 to 12. Frequency of service, measurement periods and attribution unconfirmed. Source: linkedin.md, Experience.
- F09: Chef de Partie, Brassica, Manchester, September 2016–May 2019; larder and garnish, then sauce. Source: linkedin.md, Experience.
- F10: Fjaerland Fermentation Lab, Norway, January–March 2018. No title or work description; dates overlap Brassica. Source: linkedin.md, Experience. User confirms: ten-week unpaid stage; washed and labelled jars, helped on two batches of garum. Explicitly not a researcher. Employment arrangement during the overlap remains unknown.
- F11: Diploma in Professional Cookery, Leeds Kitchen College, 2014–2016. Source: linkedin.md, Education.

## Other work, influences and testimony

- F12: Co-founder, Sunday Pot, Leeds, 2021–present; a hot meal every Sunday at St Aidan's hall, using restaurant surplus. Ines's personal duties and collaborators unspecified. Source: linkedin.md, Volunteering.
- F13: Brine: four issues, 2022–2025, about preserving. Ines writes it; drawings by friend Olu. Other contributors, publication format and reuse permissions unspecified. Sources: linkedin.md, Publications and About; notes.md, Pictures.
- F14: People ask Ines about the jar wall, koji room (a cupboard), staff meal and workshops she runs on the first Monday of the month. Workshop audience, format and availability unspecified. Source: notes.md.
- F15: Influences: The Art of Fermentation and Wild Fermentation by Sandor Katz, and her grandmother, who never measured anything. Source: notes.md.
- F16: Callum Reyes, owner of Saltmarsh, recommends: “Ines turned our bins into a larder. The best thing on the menu most weeks started as something we used to throw away.” Permission to reuse and context unconfirmed. Source: linkedin.md, Recommendations. User confirms: “Callum is happy to be quoted.” Quote reuse is approved; retain exact wording.

## Assets mentioned, not supplied

- A01: About 60 dish and jar-wall photos taken by Priya Nair for the restaurant website. Ownership, permission and credits unknown. Source: notes.md. User confirms: restaurant owns the photos; Priya Nair must be credited. Restaurant permission for portfolio reuse is not explicitly established; defer selection.
- A02: Ines's own phone photos of the larder, including labels. Restaurant permission and sensitive label content unknown. Source: notes.md. User confirms: phone photos are hers. No supplier prices or staff faces without permission. Actual photos and restaurant reuse clearance remain unreviewed.
- A03: Scans of all four Brine issues, with drawings by Olu. Reuse permissions and contributor credits unknown. Source: notes.md. User confirms: Olu owns the drawings; she will ask him before any use. Do not plan to use drawings or scans containing them until permission is recorded.
- A04: Photo of grandmother's ogiri pot. Photographer, ownership and family permission unknown. Source: notes.md. User confirms: pot photo is hers. Actual image and privacy context remain unreviewed.

## Additional confirmed facts

- F17: Audience: prospective apprentices, food writers and people booking workshops. User: “I am not looking for a job.” Booking/enquiry destinations are not supplied.
- F18: User: “Do not show supplier prices, and no faces of staff unless I have asked them.” No staff permissions have been recorded.
- F19: User works from the prep list and ferment log: jar start date, salt, check days and readiness. “The menu is the last thing written every week, not the first.” Physical document format, salt units and real entries are unknown.

## Gaps

- Intended audience and visitor action; contact destination.
- Concrete personal responsibilities at the lab and Sunday Pot; attribution of kitchen results.
- Asset files are absent; only descriptions are available.
- Everyday documents and rituals, beyond the brief mention of a prep list.
- Specific lessons from the named influences.
- Boundaries on publishing restaurant material, colleagues, family and labels.
- Whether a personal site already exists and what should happen to it.

## Disagreements

- D01: Head Chef start is March 2022 in linkedin.md; kitchen takeover is September 2022 in notes.md. These may represent different events; do not choose a date without an answer.
- D02: Brassica employment overlaps the Norway lab placement. This is not necessarily a conflict, but the relationship is unknown.

## Original questions — answer status below

1. Confirm name, current roles, listed titles/dates and education; explain March versus September 2022 and how the Norway placement fitted into Brassica.
2. Explain personal work and role at Fjaerland, and personal duties/collaborators at Sunday Pot.
3. Explain waste measurement, comparison periods and personal versus team contributions (14 to 5 kg/week).
4. Explain supplier count comparison periods, basis and personal versus team contributions (31 to 12).
5. Confirm 40 seats, weekly menu, 90-cover service frequency, basis of 40+ larder count, and whether two apprentices/year means starters or completers; identify collaborators in the larder/programme.
6. Explain Brine's publication format and own/others' contributions; workshop audience, content and current schedule.
7. Clarify permissions and credits for Priya's photos, restaurant work/phone photos/labels, Brine scans/Olu's drawings, grandmother's pot photo and Callum's quote. No permission inferred from possession.
8. Identify intended audience and desired final visitor action.
9. Identify material that must not be shown, including stories about others.
10. Name everyday documents, lists and rituals.
11. Describe lessons learned from grandmother, Katz or other influences.
12. Identify any existing personal website and desired treatment.

## User answers

Answers are recorded beside F04, F05, F10, F16, A01–A04 and F17–F19.

1. Partly answered: title dates resolved; other dates/education and stage employment arrangement unanswered.
2. Stage answered; Sunday Pot personal duties unanswered.
3. Answered for safe team wording; precise comparison windows not supplied.
4. Supplier metric unanswered; omit from concepts.
5. Capacities/count definitions and apprentice completion/intake unanswered; avoid numeric headlines.
6. Brine format/contributors and workshop detail unanswered.
7. Ownership and credit partly answered; Olu permission pending; quote approved. Restaurant reuse permission remains open.
8. Audience answered; contact/booking destinations missing.
9. Prices and faces boundaries answered; no broader permissions inferred.
10. Prep list, ferment log and menu order answered.
11. Specific lessons unanswered; do not invent lineage or lessons.
12. Existing-site status unanswered.

The original gap/disagreement lists above reflect the initial reading. F04 resolves D01; F10 partly resolves D02; F17–F19 fill audience, boundaries and working-document gaps. Remaining questions stay open. “Carry on” authorizes concepts without confirming skipped facts.
# Decisions

- Read both supplied text files and record source statements separately from confirmed facts. This keeps claims traceable. Change by correcting the fact sheet.
- Keep referenced assets unselected until authorship and reuse permission are clarified. Possession does not establish permission. Change by recording the user's specific answers.
- Create planning documents only; no code, visual concept or website implementation. The user explicitly requested planning before building.
- After the user's “Carry on”, develop concepts using confirmed prep-list/log practice while leaving skipped factual questions open. Change by supplying further facts.
- Avoid the supplier reduction metric, apprentice completion counts, invented ferment data and unapproved drawings. They add unsupported claims or permission dependencies. Change with scoped confirmation or clearance.
- Propose workshop booking and apprentice enquiry as primary end actions, writer contact secondary, because these reflect the named audiences. Change by specifying priorities and destinations.
- Keep navigation and contact visible without requiring the full scroll; require a readable static/reduced-motion presentation at storyboard stage. This preserves access to the same story. Change visual motion intensity later, without removing content access.

item.text:
**Before the menu** will be one continuous story carried by six 3D jars and their labels. The page asks: **“What happens before the menu is written?”**

The [full storyboard](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-terse-with-3SexGk/docs/story/storyboard.md) is saved. Nothing has been built.

| Chapter | What visitors learn | What moves as they scroll |
|---|---|---|
| **The log** | Your name, current role, fermentation and apprentice work, plus one scoped team result | A label unfolds onto a jar; six jars gather into a shelf |
| **Started** | Your influences and career, accurately describing the unpaid Norway stage and September 2022 title | The jars spread into a dated row, with the stage shown within the Brassica period |
| **Salt** | How the prep list and ferment log work together: start date, salt, check days, readiness | Labels face forward into a readable field diagram; one jar comes forward for an optional real example |
| **Check days** | Apprentices, workshops, *Brine* and Sunday Pot | The jars become a working shelf, highlighting one label at a time |
| **Ready** | The whole-kitchen waste measurement and Callum’s approved quote | Labels enlarge into evidence panels while the same jars remain visible |
| **The menu, written last** | The story resolves into your working documents and teaching | All six jars settle together beside workshop, apprentice and writer contact options |

The desktop sequence takes roughly ten viewport heights. Movement happens between settled reading states: small turns, translations and changes of arrangement. Scrolling remains ordinary browser scrolling. Chapter links and a contact shortcut let visitors skip directly to what matters.

The visual starting point is **warm off-white, charcoal ink and deep moss**, with simplified clear glass, restrained amber tint and matte cream labels. Source Sans 3 carries the text; IBM Plex Mono carries dates and record fields. The storyboard also includes darker “Night shelf” and pale “Label paper” treatments for later comparison.

On phones, the page becomes a single column with compact scenes or static illustrations. Reduced motion uses fixed arrangements. Without WebGL or JavaScript, visitors still get the complete text, diagrams, navigation and contact links. Important information never exists only on a rotating label.

The initial site includes a concise work index, Callum’s quote, direct contact routes, sharing metadata, a jar-and-label icon and a useful missing-page screen. Separate project pages and a blog can follow when there is enough material. I’ve planned workshop and apprentice contacts as the primary actions, with writer contact alongside them.

Your factual boundaries remain explicit: the waste result says **“we”**, includes its measurement scope, and excludes bones. No supplier prices, unauthorized staff faces, invented ferment values or unapproved Olu drawings appear. Restaurant photographs need reuse clearance and Priya’s credit.

Before final content, we need genuine contact destinations, current workshop details, and—optionally—a redacted log entry and reviewed photos. The plan works without that optional imagery. Final captions remain unwritten; the storyboard specifies their facts and purpose.

**Does this storyboard have your approval, or what should change? Approval covers the plan only.**

The [storyfolio skill](/tmp/storyfolio-evals/codex-chef-terse-with-3SexGk/.agents/skills/storyfolio/SKILL.md) requires “A yes to the script, or what to change.” That is why this final review is separate from your concept selection.
